$comment: Machine-readable verification record. Regenerate by running the commands below and updating the results. Every status here was produced by actually running the command, not by inspection.

categories.name: Formatting
categories.detail: Prettier reports all matched files conform.
categories.notes: docs/PRODUCT-SPECIFICATION.md and SETUP-CHECKLIST.md are excluded from formatting as user-authored documents. public/geo and public/maplibre are excluded: the first is Natural Earth data shipped as fetched, the second is copied from node_modules on every build.

categories.name: Linting
categories.detail: ESLint 9.39.5 flat config, next/core-web-vitals + next/typescript. Zero errors, zero warnings.
categories.notes: ESLint is pinned to the 9.x line. See knownIssues.eslint-major-pin.

categories.name: Type checking
categories.detail: tsc --noEmit clean under strict mode with noUncheckedIndexedAccess enabled.

categories.name: Unit and component tests
categories.detail: 812 tests across 49 files, all passing.

categories.name: Coverage
categories.detail: Lines 77.43%, branches 87.78%, functions 86.88%. All above configured thresholds (60/70/60).
categories.notes: Thresholds are a floor to catch accidentally-deleted tests, not a target. The deterministic core in src/core/ sits far above them; uncovered files are wiring modules (registry, factories, barrels) exercised indirectly.

categories.name: Production build
categories.detail: Next.js 16 production build succeeds. A prebuild step copies the MapLibre worker into public/maplibre so the globe can reach it.

categories.name: End-to-end smoke tests
categories.detail: 148 tests passing across desktop and mobile viewports: app shell, skip link, 404, health endpoint, PWA manifest and icons, service worker, offline page, security headers, accounts and Travel Watches, and the full discovery and search flow - homepage categories, submitting the form, restoring a search from its URL, the score explanation, the cost breakdown, the No-Surprise warnings, component swapping, result filters, flexible dates including a weekend search returning only weekends, the discovery globe and its destination pages.
categories.notes: Verified with PLAYWRIGHT_CHANNEL=chrome against locally installed Chrome. Playwright's bundled browser binary could not be downloaded in this environment. See knownIssues.playwright-browser-download. The Playwright web server runs with DATABASE_URL and REDIS_URL blanked, so the suite is hermetic and cannot write test accounts into a developer's real database.

categories.name: Accessibility
categories.detail: axe-core reports zero violations against wcag2a, wcag2aa, wcag21a and wcag21aa in both desktop and mobile viewports, on the app shell, the search page with results, the flexible-date comparison, the discovery map panel and a destination page.
categories.notes: This check found and led to fixing a real dark-mode contrast failure in status badges (2.04:1 against a 4.5:1 requirement). axe is a floor, not proof of accessibility: it cannot tell whether the cost breakdown reads sensibly in a screen reader, only that its table markup is valid. The search flow is asserted to be keyboard-operable, but no manual screen-reader pass has been done.

categories.name: Security baseline
categories.detail: CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy asserted present. X-Powered-By absent. Health endpoint asserted to contain no connection string or key-shaped value.
categories.notes: Baseline only. Authentication, rate limiting, CSRF protection and audit logging are not implemented. See docs/security.md section 9.

categories.name: Dependency audit
categories.detail: No high or critical advisories in production dependencies.
categories.notes: WARN rather than PASS because this was verified locally only. A git remote (origin) is now configured, but the workflow in .github/workflows/ci.yml has not yet run in a real runner.

categories.name: Continuous integration
categories.detail: .github/workflows/ci.yml defines four jobs: quality, build, e2e and security. Syntax is valid and every command it invokes has been run successfully locally.
categories.notes: The workflow has never executed. A git remote (origin, github.com/Inszert/VOYAGR.git) is configured, so the blocker is now only that no push has triggered a run. This becomes PASS after the first green run.

categories.name: Database layer
categories.detail: Repository interfaces implemented in memory and against PostgreSQL. All three migrations applied to a live Railway-hosted PostgreSQL 17 instance, and the same 26-test contract suite passes against both backends.
categories.notes: The suite skips the Postgres backend when TEST_DATABASE_URL is unset, and reports the skip as a skipped test, so the project keeps its property of passing with no database. Connection pooling, SSL and failure behaviour under load are untested; the instance is a development one reached over a public proxy at roughly 200ms round trip.

categories.name: Background jobs
categories.detail: Both drivers implement one contract. The in-process driver is fully tested; the BullMQ driver is tested against a live Redis 8.10.1 for round trip, deduplication, delayed jobs and - the Phase 1.6 requirement - surviving a restart of the process that enqueued the work. The worker boots against live Redis and PostgreSQL, sweeps due watches and refreshes them.
categories.notes: Queue tests create and then obliterate uniquely named queues, so they touch nothing already on the instance. Behaviour under worker crash mid-job, Redis failover and multi-worker contention is untested.

categories.name: AI boundary
categories.detail: 19 tests covering schema validation, cross-field rules, deterministic budget conversion, invented-figure detection and graceful degradation.
categories.notes: Verified against the deterministic mock provider only. No live model has been run through these guardrails; prompt-injection resistance is untested against a real LLM.

categories.name: PWA foundation
categories.detail: Manifest valid and served, all three declared icons served as real PNGs, service worker served with a must-revalidate policy, offline page renders.
categories.notes: Service worker registration and runtime caching behaviour have not been exercised in a browser — the worker is disabled in development by design, and the E2E suite asserts the file is served rather than that it installs and caches. Install-to-homescreen and push delivery are untested.

categories.name: Manual change review
categories.detail: All created and modified files inspected before completion. No existing file was deleted or overwritten; docs/PRODUCT-SPECIFICATION.md and SETUP-CHECKLIST.md are untouched. Git history preserved. The bootstrap was subsequently reviewed and committed as f9b7cba.

categories.name: Search orchestration (Phase 1.1)
categories.detail: 75 tests covering date arithmetic, the shared concurrency limiter, search planning, candidate assembly and orchestration. Asserted: a search returns ranked, costed, constrained candidates from mocks; each of the four adapters failing in turn degrades the result set rather than aborting the search; an adapter that throws instead of returning a Result is handled identically; a partially failing hotel provider loses only its own destination; results are deterministic across runs; every limit bounds the fan-out; the concurrency bound is reached but never exceeded across the whole nested fan-out, and tightening it changes the pace but not the answer; a wrong-currency quote is dropped rather than converted.
categories.notes: Verified against deterministic mocks only. Real provider latency, rate limiting, pagination and partial-response behaviour are untested, and the per-call timeout is unproven against a live API. Default limits imply up to 8 flight calls and 48 hotel calls per search, paced at 6 concurrent; that budget is a guess until a vendor is chosen. Covered by the live-provider readiness task in docs/implementation-plan.md. Search results are cached for five minutes at the page level and the age is displayed; runSearch itself is uncached, so a background refresh always hits the providers.

categories.name: Search UI and structured schema (Phase 1.2)
categories.detail: 47 tests. The structured schema is asserted to normalise airport codes, convert budgets to Money in minor units, read an absent checkbox as false, keep optional numbers null rather than zero, and reject fourteen kinds of bad input with a message on the offending field. The booking seam is asserted to drop javascript:, data:, file: and non-URL deep links, and to mark every outbound link noopener and sponsored. Components are asserted on roles and accessible names: estimates labelled in words, excluded costs surfaced, warnings visible without expanding anything, violations listed on a near miss, and the results heading reporting what matched rather than what is shown.
categories.notes: No standalone trip detail route exists, by design — see the note in docs/implementation-plan.md 1.2. Place names come from provider fixtures via src/search/destination-names.ts, a marked stand-in for the destinations table (specification section 21); it is display-only and no computed figure reads it. The page is server-rendered on every request with no caching, which is correct against instant mocks and will need revisiting when a live provider makes a search cost money.

categories.name: Data honesty fixes
categories.detail: Flight times are a LocalDateTime distinct from an instant: a Z-suffixed or offset-bearing flight time is rejected, the clock face is read through one helper rather than through Date, and a test asserts a candidate carrying a UTC-claiming flight time is refused rather than silently misread. Baggage and self-transfer are boolean | null: an unstated fact does not satisfy a hard requirement, produces a needs_verification warning rather than a false denial, takes half the scoring penalty, and lowers data confidence. Asserted end to end against a provider that prices flights without stating what is included.
categories.notes: The mock flight provider always states its facts, so the unknown path is exercised by unit tests and by a purpose-built terse provider in the orchestrator suite rather than by the standard fixtures. Whether a real vendor omits a field, sends an empty string or sends a misleading default is a per-vendor mapping question, tracked in the live-provider readiness task.

categories.name: Price history (Phase 1.7)
categories.detail: Every refresh records the trip total and each priced component with full provenance: who quoted it, when we observed it, in what currency and under what conditions. Asserted: no transfer row rather than a zero when none was priced, the total attributed to the cost engine rather than to one provider, the quoted-versus-estimated share recorded as a condition, history accumulating across runs, and the lowest total queryable per currency. Verified end to end against live PostgreSQL and Redis: a due watch was enqueued, refreshed and wrote four observations.
categories.notes: Every refresh writes a row whether or not the price moved, which is deliberate - "it did not change" is information - but it means no retention policy exists yet and the table grows without bound. Presentation of the history, and deciding whether a change is worth an alert, are Phase 1.8 and Phase 2.

categories.name: Web Push delivery (Phase 1.9)
categories.command: manual: real browser against live Postgres, Redis and FCM
categories.detail: A real Chrome profile subscribed via fcm.googleapis.com; the worker detected a drop with the real deal detector, queued delivery through BullMQ, and web-push delivered it. The browser received the push and it deep-linked back to the originating search. The notification row was stamped delivered.
categories.notes: Proven once, by hand, with a seeded prior price observation standing in for an earlier dearer run. Not part of npm test: it needs VAPID keys, a real push service and a non-incognito browser profile, none of which belong in a suite that must pass with no external services. The Playwright suite runs with the keys blanked so it behaves the same on any machine. Delivery to Safari/APNs and to Firefox is untested.

categories.name: Worker housekeeping
categories.detail: The worker sweeps expired sessions every six hours and prunes price observations older than 90 days daily. Asserted on both backends: a live session is never swept, and the cheapest observation per watch, component and currency survives pruning whatever its age.
categories.notes: Price-history retention is the policy docs/security.md requires before launch, for that table only. Account deletion and the rest of a user's data still have no answer.

knownIssues.summary: ESLint pinned to the 9.x line, which upstream marks end-of-life.
knownIssues.cause: eslint-config-next@16.3.5 bundles an eslint-plugin-react version that calls a context API removed in ESLint 10, producing 'contextOrFilename.getFilename is not a function'.
knownIssues.impact: Development-only dependency; not in the production dependency tree.
knownIssues.resolution: Upgrade when Next.js ships ESLint 10 support.

knownIssues.summary: Playwright's bundled Chromium and ffmpeg could not be downloaded in this environment.
knownIssues.cause: The Playwright CDN was unreachable (repeated TLS timeouts).
knownIssues.impact: None on assertions. The suite was verified against locally installed Chrome via PLAYWRIGHT_CHANNEL=chrome. Video capture is opt-in via PLAYWRIGHT_VIDEO=1 since it needs the missing ffmpeg.
knownIssues.resolution: Run 'npx playwright install chromium' on a machine with CDN access. CI installs it normally.

knownIssues.summary: Content-Security-Policy allows 'unsafe-inline' for scripts and styles.
knownIssues.cause: Next.js streaming style and script injection currently requires it.
knownIssues.resolution: Move to a nonce-based CSP before handling payments or authenticated mutations.

requiresUserAction: Push to origin so GitHub Actions runs for the first time; the workflow is still unproven in a real runner.
Run 'npx playwright install chromium' on a network that can reach the Playwright CDN, to use bundled Chromium instead of local Chrome.
Approve the Playwright MCP server in .mcp.json when prompted; project MCP servers are not enabled automatically.
Revisit the default search limits in src/search/types.ts against the chosen provider's rate limit and price list before Phase 1.11.
Decide the flight and hotel provider vendors before Phase 1.11.
Decide the LLM vendor before AI explanations go live.
Decide PostgreSQL hosting before Phase 1.4 and Redis hosting before Phase 1.6.
Choose a licence; README records it as not yet chosen.
Decide where the search cache should live once more than one server instance runs: it is in-process today, so two instances keep two caches. Redis arrives with Phase 1.6.
